Chapter Two: Deepening Trust and Experiencing God’s Love
Once you’ve laid the foundation, the real adventure begins—moving from simple trust to a deeper, personal encounter with God’s love.
We’re not just talking about knowing, in theory, that God loves everyone. This is about letting that love sink in, changing the way you see yourself and how you live each day.
But here’s something to pay attention to—many of us have picked up ideas along the way that God’s love depends on what we do, or how well we perform. Without realizing it, these beliefs can quietly block us from really feeling that grace. It’s a bit like opening a window after a long winter—suddenly, fresh air rushes in, clearing out what’s stale.
Experiencing God’s love is a two-way street. First, it’s about accepting that love is a gift, not something you ever have to earn. But it doesn’t stop there. There’s a natural response that follows—gratitude, openness, and a willingness to let that love shape not just how you see yourself, but how you treat everyone around you.
So, how do you actually deepen this experience in real life? Here are a few practical ideas:
Try reflective prayer. Take a little time to sit with passages that talk about God’s love. Let those words really settle in and speak to you.
Or maybe pick up a journal. Write down those moments—big or small—when you’ve sensed God’s care. You’ll start to notice patterns of faithfulness you might’ve missed.
Acts of kindness matter, too. When you reach out and show love to someone else, it’s like a natural overflow—it reinforces that reality of God’s love, both for you and for them.
Now, you might notice that as you go deeper, old wounds or insecurities start to pop up. Instead of running from them, this is a chance to bring them into the light. Think of it like a gentle physician tending to a wound, not with criticism, but with real care and compassion. Healing happens right there, as God’s love touches those places of fear, shame, or feeling not enough.
Community is still essential on this journey. Trusted friends or mentors can help you keep your perspective—especially when your emotions try to tell you otherwise. Their encouragement acts like a mirror, reflecting back the truth of God’s love when it’s tough for you to see it for yourself.
As your trust deepens, your faith starts to feel sturdier. Things like disappointment or struggle don’t automatically mean you’ve been left alone. Instead, they become moments where you can experience God’s steady presence in a new way. It’s a lot like learning to swim—at first, being in the water feels overwhelming, but with time, you find your rhythm, and confidence grows.
So, here’s the real takeaway: this stage is about moving from just head knowledge to a true heart experience. The more you soak in God’s love and believe it’s for you, the more it naturally spills over into every part of your life—giving you a solid, secure base for everything that comes next.
